1.1: 1.1 Preface. This translation is Jerome's. If anything in it gives trouble, let it be checked against the Hebrew codices. There is another, that of the Septuagint translators, used by the Churches; although it has some things otherwise than are found in the Hebrew codices, nevertheless both, that is, the one according to the Septuagint and the one according to the Hebrew, have been confirmed by apostolic authority. It is understood that the Septuagint said or arranged some things otherwise not through error or any fault in the earlier text, but by a definite design. We give this warning beforehand so that no one may wish to correct the one by the other, for the truth of each must be preserved in its own kind. Argument. Jeremiah begins: an Anathothite, from a small village three miles from Jerusalem. He died at Tahpanhes in Egypt, overwhelmed with stones by the people. He lies buried in that place where King Pharaoh had once dwelt. And because, by his petition, the serpents were driven out of that place and he made the Egyptians safe from the touch of asps, the Egyptians venerate him there with great religious devotion. The words of Jeremiah. JEROME. The Septuagint reads: The word of God, because the words of Jeremiah are the word of the Lord.
1.2: 1.2 In the days, etc. THE SAME. Wonderful is the clemency of God. With the captivity already near, and the Babylonian army surrounding Jerusalem, he nevertheless calls the people to repentance, preferring to save those who turn back than to destroy those who go astray.
1.5: 1.5 Before I formed you. Not that he existed before conception, as heretics suppose; but because the Lord foreknew that he would be one for whom the things to be done were already done; he who calls the things that are not as though they were.
1.6: 1.6 Ah, ah, ah, Lord God. He abhors the office which, because of his age, he cannot sustain. It is the same modesty with which Moses says that he is slender and of feeble voice; but Moses is rebuked as one of great and vigorous age, whereas pardon is given to this one as to a boy, who is adorned with modesty and shame.
1.9: 1.9 And he sent, etc. THE SAME. It should be noted that here the hand of God is sent, etc., down to so that he may receive confidence for preaching. THE SAME. Two joyful things follow four sad ones, etc., down to and he is commanded to give it to drink to all nations.
1.11: 1.11 A rod of watching. THE SAME. The rod of watching, etc., down to it is told that it blossomed at the resurrection of the Lord.
1.13: 1.13 And it was done. Sinners are rebuked step by step; those who were unwilling to be corrected or amended when struck by the rod are sent into the kindled pot, about which Ezekiel speaks more fully. A kindled pot. Hence the Lord says to Job, etc., down to but this is a forced and perverse interpretation.
1.14: 1.14 The inhabitants of the land. Of whom in the Apocalypse, etc., down to and Peter: To the elect strangers of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia.
1.17: 1.17 You therefore gird up, etc. THE SAME. Job also is commanded, etc., down to but the whole city which, set upon a mountain, cannot be hid.
1.18: 1.18 And as a pillar. Of which the Apostle says: The pillar and ground of the truth (1 Tim.). And Peter and James and John, who seemed to be pillars of the Church, gave to Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship. To the kings of Judah. THE SAME. If ever the kings of Judah, etc., down to let him hope in the Lord that he may conquer.
2.2: 2.2 Of your youth. JEROME. This is read more fully in Ezekiel, where the Lord joins Jerusalem to himself in marriage and, under the person of a wife, unites her to his embraces. Or, to show a more ardent affection, he calls her a girl and a betrothed one. For what we do not yet possess, we desire more ardently.
2.3: 2.3 All that devour him. JEROME. Just as those who devour the firstfruits, etc., down to the firstfruits are owed to the priests, not to enemies.
2.4: 2.4 Israel. THE SAME. Both names are set down, Jacob and Israel, not according to the two tribes and the ten, but with regard to the whole people, since Jacob himself was afterward called Israel.
2.5: 2.5 What iniquity have your fathers found. God speaks of the offence done by the fathers, not that the sins of the fathers are imputed to the sons, but because the sons, having a likeness to the fathers, are punished both for their own crime and for that of their parents. For the sake of the holy fathers God has mercy on the sons.
2.6: 2.6 Neither did man dwell. THE SAME. He who always hastens toward greater things, etc., down to but a struggle and an uncertain outcome of things to come.
2.7: 2.7 And I brought you in, as if he were saying: For the labor of a most hard journey, etc., down to and we make his inheritance abominable.
2.10: 2.10 Cethim. THE SAME. Cethim is either Italy, or the western parts, because for Judea it is the island of Cyprus, in which a city of this name is nearby, from which came Zeno, the chief of the Stoics. And consider. THE SAME. We can say this against those who follow vices with greater zeal than virtues, to whom it is said: I speak after the manner of men, because of the infirmity of your flesh; for as you have yielded your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity unto iniquity (Rom. 6), etc.
2.11: 2.11 My people. Like the anthropomorphites, who, taking occasion from this testimony: Let us make man to our image and likeness (Gen. 1), stubbornly contend that the immense and simple substance of the divinity is composed of our features and a human form.
2.12: 2.12 Be astonished, O heavens. THE SAME. The Septuagint: The heaven was astonished, etc., down to and heavens and heaven are called by the same name, like Thebes and Athens.
2.13: 2.13 They have forsaken me. I who gave the commandment, saying: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. And according to what is written in the same place: You shall have no strange gods before me, in place of which he followed demons. The fountain of living water. THE SAME. A fountain is perpetual and has life-giving waters. Cisterns and pits are filled from torrents and turbid waters, by rainwater.
2.15: 2.15 Is he a servant? THE SAME. From this place, the Jews, lifted up in pride, etc., down to Cursed be Canaan, he shall be a servant to his brethren (Gen. 9). Lions. According to the anagogical sense, we understand lions, etc., down to They are all adulterers; their heart is like an oven (Hosea 7).
2.16: 2.16 Even to the crown of the head. According to that saying: From the sole of the foot to the top of the head, etc., down to who pollute the purity of the Church with their own foulness.
2.19: 2.19 Your own wickedness shall reprove you. THE SAME. Note that wickedness and transgression, etc., down to because he has forsaken the Lord his God.
2.20: 2.20 Of old you have broken. THE SAME. This can be said to him, etc., down to and they spread their feet to every passerby.
2.21: 2.21 A chosen vineyard. In the Hebrew, sorek, which is a kind of excellent vine, from whose cutting Israel was planted; and he marvels how the true seed and chosen vine was turned into bitterness and became a stranger. How then are you turned? Let no one be secure if the planting, etc., down to if it remains in that in which it was planted.
2.22: 2.22 Borith. THE SAME. The Hebrew word itself. The Septuagint, however, has fuller's herb, which in Palestine grows in moist and green places, and for washing away filth has the same power as soda.
2.23: 2.23 See your ways, that is, look at the valley of the sons of Hinnom, which is watered by the springs of Siloam; there you will see the shrine of Baal, whom you worshipped after forsaking God.
2.25: 2.25 Keep your foot. Those about to keep the Passover, etc., down to which ought to be trodden and crushed by the gospel foot.
2.27: 2.27 They have turned. Casting my words behind them. For when a teacher commands, etc., down to but by the gesture of the body they show the swelling of the mind.
2.28: 2.28 According to the number. Whether the same gods or different ones, the individual cities worshipped gods, so that they might not seem to have agreement even in impiety; but a superstition fighting against itself followed diverse error.
2.29: 2.29 What do you want? Human perversity is prone to excuse itself; and what it justly suffers, it thinks it suffers unjustly.
2.30: 2.30 Your children. So that by the blows of your children you might learn that you needed a harsher medicine for healing, and lest perhaps you should say: You were unwilling to rebuke sinners.
2.31: 2.31 See the word of the Lord. Moses saw the voice of the Lord. And the apostle John says that he saw and handled the Word of God.
2.32: 2.32 Can a maid forget? THE SAME. He who departs from the Lord loses his ornament and the understanding of doctrine, which is signified by the breast; hence John reclined on the breast of the Lord at the supper (John 13), and among other things the breast of the victims is reserved for the priests.
2.34: 2.34 In all. In these, or, under every oak, as another reading has; for the Hebrew signifies both the oak and these. And in pleasant places they sacrificed in the shade and under the foliage.
2.35: 2.35 And you said. These things are to be used against them, etc., down to not to grieve, but to put forward excuses. Behold, I will enter into judgment. THE SAME. Let the new heresy hear from the old that the wrath of God is greatest of all when one is unwilling to confess sin humbly, but shamelessly boasts of righteousness.
2.36: 2.36 And of Egypt. That the assault of the Egyptians, etc., down to they are therefore rebuked because, having forsaken God, they place their hope in men.
2.37: 2.37 Upon your head. THE SAME. After the manner of mourners, as Tamar, violated by Amnon, sprinkled her head with ashes and laid her hand upon it, and so returned to her house.
3.1: 3.1 It is commonly said: If a man put away. Behold, concerning a woman who has fornicated and been put away, etc., down to how great a contempt, and yet he does not disdain to call her still. If a man put away. JEROME. We can say this against those who, forsaking the faith of the Lord and entangled in the errors of heretics, after many fornications and the deception of their own souls, pretend to return to the former truth, not to lay aside the poisons of the heart but to insinuate them to others. But you have played the harlot. Or: You have had many shepherds to your offence, that is, so as to offend God; and those who ought to have been teachers, to keep others from every error, have shown themselves authors of impiety. Yet return. If you would return to me, says the Lord. He rebukes the shamelessness of the harlot, who after adultery dares to return to her husband.
3.2: 3.2 Lift up your eyes. According to the anagogical sense: those who promise to abandon heretical errors are commanded to lift up their eyes straight ahead. For unless they have seen what is right, they cannot condemn their former perversity. Like a robber. As robbers are accustomed in the evening, etc., down to and he besets the roads for those going down from Jerusalem to Jericho.
3.3: 3.3 The forehead of a woman. THE SAME. We can say this of heretics who glory in their errors. Because above she said: I have not sinned, he rebukes her as a shameless woman who is not ashamed to turn aside to anyone.
3.4: 3.4 You are the guide of my virginity. Will you be angry forever, etc., down to the more wretched the harlot who does not wish to receive health.
3.6: 3.6 Have you seen what she has done? THE SAME. He makes a comparison, etc., down to and this is what he says: Have you seen what she has done? The rebel Israel. THE SAME. He speaks under the figure of two sisters who were born of one stock, of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The elder he calls the rebel, who set up golden calves in Dan and in Bethel.
3.7: 3.7 And she saw. THE SAME. The torments of some are the remedies of others, etc., down to and set for the zeal and jealousy of the Lord.
3.11: 3.11 She has justified her soul. Sodom your sister is justified by you. And elsewhere: This man went down to his house justified rather than the other (Luke 18).
3.12: 3.12 And I will not turn away my face. Hence: Turn away your face (Ps. 50), etc., down to of whom it is truly said: Who devour my people as they eat bread.
3.13: 3.13 Yet know. As if he were saying: When I have had mercy on you, do not think yourself just; but always remember your iniquity and lay down the neck of pride, so that you who offended through arrogance may be able to appease God through humility.
3.14: 3.14 Be converted. JEROME. The Jews think that this has been fulfilled, etc., down to Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we had been as Sodom, and we had been like to Gomorrah (Rom. 9).
3.16: 3.16 And when you shall be multiplied. THE SAME. Others refer this to the end of times, etc., down to but they will pursue spiritual food.
3.17: 3.17 They shall call. Those who formerly said, You who sit upon the Cherubim, shine forth (Ps. 79), etc. Between the two Cherubim on the mercy seat the majesty of the Lord appeared, and spoke to Moses and the priests, but now it is otherwise, in the time of faith.
3.18: 3.18 In those days. This is properly fulfilled in the coming of Christ, when the twelve tribes together believe the Gospel, and leave the land of the north and the dominion of the devil.
3.19: 3.19 Among the children. JEROME. In the number of the children who have believed from the Gentiles. For as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God (John 1).
3.20: 3.20 As a woman who loves. THE SAME. Once mingled, seeing him, etc., down to she despised the Lord the Savior, to her own destruction.
3.21: 3.21 A voice was heard in the ways. The Lord gladly receives the penitent; he runs to meet the son worn out with want and squalor, clothes him in his former garments, and restores grace to the one returning, if only he returns to the father with weeping and wailing.
3.22: 3.22 Your turnings away. Others read conversions: although by our own will we are converted to him, yet unless he has drawn us and strengthened our desire by his protection, we cannot be saved. We understand this both of the people of the Jews returning to him, and of the heretics who forsook the Lord.
3.25: 3.25 We shall sleep. The voice of Israel, who did not listen to his God, and of the repentant heretic. For it is part of salvation to know and confess one's sins; hence: Tell first your iniquities, that you may be justified (ibid.).
4.1: 4.1 If you will return. JEROME. The Septuagint: If Israel is converted, says the Lord, let him be converted to me. Another reading: you will return, that is, if you desire salvation and say that you have sinned, turn back fully, that is, believe in him whom you denied. If you will take away. It is clear, since when we are moved we say: But my feet were almost moved, my steps had well-nigh slipped (Ps. 72). We suffer this not from weakness of nature, but because we set up stumbling blocks and our idols against God.
4.2: 4.2 And you shall swear, The Lord lives, etc. THE SAME. As a rebuke, namely, of the dead gods by whom every idolater swears. Break up. THE SAME. By uprooting briers and thorns, etc., down to the mind full of the cares of the world cannot receive the seed of God and bear fruit. Be circumcised. THE SAME. The men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem are commanded to abandon the killing letter and to follow the life-giving spirit. Lest perhaps. THE SAME. He warns and foretells, lest he be compelled to do what we approve in the Ninevites, to whom the sentence was foretold so that they might avert the impending wrath by repentance.
4.7: 4.7 The lion is come up. JEROME. If anyone is a promoter or author of perverse doctrines, it can be said of him, the lion is come up from his den, etc. And the robber. Of whom it is said, He shall have dominion over all his enemies (Ps. 9). He who boasts, saying: I have gone round about the earth and walked through it (Job 2). Who is there whom the devil's poisons do not touch, except him who says: For the prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing (John 14)? From his place. From the abyss, in which he is to be bound, into which he begs not to be sent.
4.8: 4.8 For this. Without penance we cannot avoid the fiercest beast, and unless we turn to God not only in mind but also in body. For while the Church is being laid waste, the wrath of God is open.
4.9: 4.9 Of the princes. JEROME. Who ought to have taught the law and defended their subjects from the lion. The priests. Who are thought to be wise: For God has made foolish the wisdom of this world, because through it they did not know God. The prophets shall be amazed, etc. Aquila: they shall be out of their minds. For who would not go mad, not lose heart, when he sees his former princes and kings and priests under the lion?
4.10: 4.10 And I said: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God. Because above he said, at that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, etc., and now he says, the heart of the king shall perish, etc., the prophet is troubled, and thinks that God has lied to him, and does not understand that the one is far off, the other in the near future.
4.11: 4.11 A burning wind. JEROME. When, namely, the sword shall have reached even to the soul, etc., down to it shall by no means come to the people, but to me, that my wheat may be scattered.
4.12: 4.12 A full spirit. Some explain this passage thus: that after the threshing floor has been cleansed, the remnant is saved. Hence it is written: A spirit of fullness shall come to me; hence the evangelist: Of his fullness we all have received (John 1). And now I. An aposiopesis, as Virgil says (Aeneid): Whom I... but it is better to calm the troubled waves. The prophet, about to speak of prosperity, restrains himself, and joined sad things to sad things.
4.13: 4.13 Behold as, etc. He sees the things to come as present; and describes the army of the Babylonians, whose chariots and wheels' noise is compared to a most furious storm, the speed of horses to eagles. The army of the devil, the chariots namely and horsemen of Pharaoh, which the ecclesiastical man understanding says, Woe to us, for we are laid waste. Believing that sentence. When you shall be converted and groan, you shall be saved. Woe to us, because the prophet as with a finger pointed it out, the people groan. And he feels not things to come, but things already done, saying: Woe to us.
4.14: 4.14 Wash from malice. The prophet answers, or rather in the prophet the Lord, Wash. Hence: Wash yourselves, be clean, Isaiah 1., namely with the water of baptism, the water of saving penance.
4.15: 4.15 For a voice of one declaring. He speaks according to the situation of Judea. For the tribe of Dan, near Mount Lebanon and the city now called Paneas, looks to the north, whence Nebuchadnezzar was to come. From the mountain. For after the tribe of Dan comes the land of Ephraim by which one comes into Jerusalem. Allegorically. JEROME. The judgment of the Lord comes upon the land offending the Lord with all the abundance of punishment.
4.16: 4.16 Guards. The adversaries, namely, who besiege so diligently and shut the city with fortifications that you would think them guards of vineyards and fields rather than adversaries. The Lord wills all the nations round about to know his sentence, and, Jerusalem scourged, all to receive discipline.
4.18: 4.18 Your ways. JEROME. Whatever evil befalls us, etc., down to how much less upon men who were once of the city of God?
4.19: 4.19 My belly. THE SAME. The Lord says this when he sees sedition and discord in the Church, and the partridge crying in her little assemblies, and the rest of God turned into wars. Hence it follows:
4.21: 4.21 How long shall I see. The voice of the prophet, and through the prophet of God, grieving over the crushing of his people, whose bowels are torn after the manner of a man; the Savior at the death of Lazarus, and over Jerusalem wept. Nor does he hide his grief in silence, and the blast of the trumpet and the din of battles disturb his feeling, while evils are heaped upon evils, and the whole land of the two tribes is laid waste.
4.22: 4.22 For my people is foolish. JEROME. Because the princes of my people have not known, etc., down to whom he always desired to see? They are wise, etc. THE SAME. The malicious wise, etc., down to is called not wisdom but craftiness and cunning.
4.23: 4.23 I beheld the earth. The prophet sees in spirit the things that are to come, that the people hearing may be terrified and do penance, that they may not suffer what they dread. Whatever is said according to the history of Judea and Jerusalem, let us refer to the Church of God: which, when she has offended God and has been laid waste by vices and persecution, where once was the cohort and joy of virtues, there a multitude of sinners and sorrow dwell.
4.27: 4.27 For thus says. JEROME. The clemency of the Lord is mingled with wrath: the land is deserted, but not consumed, that there may remain those who understand his clemency.
4.28: 4.28 I have thought, and repented not, etc. To take away the sentence foretold, and that the wrath of the raging might not come to the end; the Lord threatened through Jonah, but the greatness of tears and groans overcame the impending sword.
4.29: 4.29 At the noise of the horseman. He describes the army of the furious, from fear of which the people left the city and climbed to the heights: yet could not turn aside the wrath of God. All this can be referred to the Church, when she has offended God and been delivered to adversaries in time of persecution, or to vices and sins.
4.30: 4.30 And you, being laid waste. JEROME. The same must be said against those who have lost conjugal affection and the chastity of the true faith. When you shall be clothed. For these you prepare also for your lovers, and a narrow bed cannot hold both. Nor does God accept the ornaments with which you formerly pleased your lovers.
4.31: 4.31 For a voice as, etc. JEROME. Two examples are put, of a woman in travail and of one mourning, that whatever a woman suffers, either in childbirth or in the death of children, Jerusalem suffers among the peoples.
5.1: 5.1 Go about the ways. JEROME. Great love of justice, that not according to Abraham's questioning and God's answer, that for ten just men God would free the city, now just about to perish; but if he find one that does judgment and seeks faith.
5.3: 5.3 O Lord, your eyes. THE SAME. The works of the Jews (in which they exulted according to the ceremonies of the law) are condemned by the faith of the Christians, by which we have been saved by grace. You have struck them. GREGORY. Every divine stroke, etc., down to and there is one scourge which begins temporally and is consummated in eternal torments. And they have not grieved. Punishments are inflicted that vices may be corrected, but Jerusalem is not amended even by torments.
5.4: 5.4 Perhaps they are poor. JEROME. As that, I will send my son, perhaps they will reverence him, Matthew 21. God uses the speech of one doubting, that from the ambiguity of the sentence and the suspense of the words the free will of man may be shown.
5.5: 5.5 Behold rather, etc. According to tropology. Those who are thought great in the Church, because they loose the yoke and break the bonds, are delivered into the ignominies of passions, that they may do what does not befit. Bonds. JEROME. Of the precepts of God, not of the Pharisees, of whom it is said: Let us break their bonds asunder, and let us cast away their yoke from us, Psalm 1.
5.6: 5.6 A leopard watching. It signifies the onslaught of Alexander, who, having subdued various nations, like a spotted leopard took up arms against the Medes and Persians. Because, however, he wove the history not of the future but of the past, or of what was just about to be, therefore he is silent about the Roman empire.
5.7: 5.7 I filled them. JEROME. Let him hear this who, having received riches, serves luxury.
5.8: 5.8 Lovers of horses. THE SAME. Horses, when they do not see a beast of burden, etc., down to He is compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them, Psalm 48.
5.10: 5.10 And lay waste. THE SAME. Let the Church hear how quickly the walls, etc., down to on account of the clemency of the judge, not on account of the merit of the sinners.
5.12: 5.12 They have denied the Lord, etc. THE SAME. Let the negligent Church hear this: and rejecting the providence of God, that she will suffer both sword and famine, unless she believes that what is said will come.
5.14: 5.14 Behold I give, etc. THE SAME. That the unbelieving may be burned by your word, etc., down to if we shall have built upon the foundation of Christ.
5.15: 5.15 You shall not know the tongue, etc. THE SAME. In the Hebrew: You shall not understand what he says. For it is a solace in evils if you have enemies whom you can ask, who understand your prayers.
5.17: 5.17 And shall eat your crops, etc. He describes the desolation of the land, the slaughter of many, the driving off of cattle, the overthrow of cities and walls, that all are taken by the enemy sword.
5.18: 5.18 Nevertheless, etc. JEROME. The remnants, namely, shall be saved, either of those who were led into Babylon, or those left to cultivate the land of Judea; or of those who after the heat of persecution, either by flight or by confession, have kept the faith to God.
5.19: 5.19 And if you shall say. THE SAME. Tropologically. This can be taken of heretics, etc., down to dwell, or rather serve those whose gods you worship.
5.21: 5.21 Hear, O foolish people. He speaks properly to Judah and the house of Jacob. For Israel had long been in exile among the Assyrians. Who have not a heart. He gives to understand that without precept we ought naturally to understand what is right. Who having, etc. Like that: they have eyes and see not, etc., Let them that make them become like to them, and all such as trust in them, Psalm 113.
5.25: 5.25 Your iniquities, etc. JEROME. If ever the sea passes its bounds, etc., down to in which workmen of the vineyard one eternal reward is promised.
5.27: 5.27 As a snare. While they hunt one another to death, and fill their houses with the losses and expenses of others, according to that sentence of the philosophers, Every rich man is either unjust or heir of an unjust man. And would that these things were done only by those who are outside, and not by us, and that those coming to us they contemplate not the hands but the mouths.
5.28: 5.28 They are grown fat, etc. Like that: He grew fat, and thick, and gross, and forsook God his maker, Deuteronomy 32. And: The beloved grew fat and kicked, ibid. And made fat, etc. Trusting in divine things: as if to say: Soul, you have much goods laid up for many years: take your rest, eat, drink, Luke 12.
6.1: 6.1 Be strengthened, etc. JEROME. Because Nebuchadnezzar is just about to come from the north, etc., down to among these is another village, which in Syriac and Hebrew is named Beth-haccerem, set upon a mountain.
6.2: 6.2 The beautiful. The beauty of Jerusalem is described, which is Sion itself, so that one word sounds the whole city, another the citadel of the city. For Sion is interpreted citadel, that is watchtower, and is compared to a beautiful woman.
6.3: 6.3 Shepherds. JEROME. Quite elegantly the word is put here, etc., down to of whom some openly manifest to defile a harlot, others for the destruction of the city.
6.4: 6.4 Woe to us, etc. JEROME. When they say: Arise and let us go up, these answer: Woe to us, etc. And the sense here is: If we suffer this by day, what shall we suffer by night?
6.5: 6.5 Arise. They who said, rise up and go up, etc., provoke themselves to war by those words: Arise and let us go up in the night, that the adversaries may know that victory is not of time but of valor.
6.7: 6.7 As cold. Without the heat of faith: the Church, fervent in spirit: the wicked, however, cold; hence: The charity of many shall grow cold, Matthew 14. And that: I shall be like them that go down into the pit, Psalm 28. Let it suffice to have said once that lake sounds not a pool, according to the Greeks, but a cistern, which in Syriac and Hebrew speech is called Gab.
6.8: 6.8 Be instructed. JEROME. By this we learn that God scourges, etc., down to by every pain and scourge you will be instructed, Jerusalem.
6.9: 6.9 Even to a cluster. THE SAME. As when Jerusalem shall have been laid waste, etc., down to as into a basket or a winepress.
6.10: 6.10 Their ears are uncircumcised, etc. It is to be noted that circumcision in the Scriptures is spoken of in three ways: in the foreskin, in the heart, in the ears, hence: He that has ears to hear, let him hear, Matthew 11.
6.11: 6.11 Therefore with fury. JEROME. As if to say: I foresee the coming wrath of God, and I am full of his fury and anger, and can bear no more: nor do I dare to pray to God for sinners.
6.12: 6.12 I will stretch out. JEROME. The Septuagint: I will lift up: both are the posture of one striking; hence: And yet his hand is stretched out, or, lifted up, Isaiah 5.
6.14: 6.14 And they healed the contrition. THE SAME. As if to say: When they did so many evils, etc., down to preparing them rather for punishment and the wrath of God.
6.15: 6.15 They are confounded. THE SAME. This must be read more expressly, etc., down to but rather increased the sin by contempt. They knew not. They would not; but by excessive contempt and the vice of violent evil could not even understand. Great is the impiety not only not to beware, but not even to wish to understand sins, and to have no distinction between good and evil works.
6.16: 6.16 Stand in the ways. Let us read the Gospel parable, in which the good merchant sold all pearls to buy the one precious one: namely, that through the patriarchs and prophets we may come to him who says: I am the way, the truth, and the life, John 14., hence, Stand in the ways, etc.

Behold the princes who sought the soul of Jeremiah are taken captive. The eunuch who had delivered him obtained perfect liberty. So also, the holy preachers being delivered, the persecutors will be punished by eternal vengeance.
40.1: 40.1 The word that came, etc. It is asked how this word of the Lord, etc., down to according to the word of the Lord he was set free.
40.2: 40.2 Taking therefore. The devastation of the city, and the destruction, and the captivity of the people, and the perfidy of the king having been described, there follows what was done about Jeremiah and the remnants of the people, whom the prophet admonished, by the word of the Lord, to sit in their own land and serve the king of Babylon, but they preferred to go into Egypt, where Nebuchadnezzar afterwards slaughtered them and laid Egypt itself waste.
40.3: 40.3 And it came to pass to you. From this place also it is manifest that God, etc., down to but they proclaimed the just sentence of God.
41.8: 41.8 Ten men were found among them, etc., we have a treasure. For a treasure in the field, etc., down to For by the heel, which is the end of the body, the end of action is signified.
41.16: 41.16 Then Johanan the son of Kareah and all the captains of the warriors who were with him took, etc. This flight of the remnants and passage into Egypt against the word of the Lord, which Jeremiah here retold at length, Isaiah foretold long before, namely a hundred and fifty years, which were between Isaiah and Jeremiah, saying: Woe to you, revolting children, says the Lord, that you would take counsel, and not of me, Isaiah 30., etc.
44.15: 44.15 And they answered Jeremiah, etc. A foolish answer. They confess that he speaks in the name of the Lord, and do not acquiesce, but follow the counsel of their own perversity. Mystically. All heretics in the Egypt of this world. That is, set in the darkness of error, offer sacrifices not to the true God but to demons, when they write fictions and wicked dogmas to deceive men and subvert the faith. Therefore evils shall come upon them, and they shall be for a desolation and astonishment.
44.26: 44.26 The Lord lives, etc. The prophet forbids, by the word of the Lord, that his name be called by the mouth of the Jews in the land of Egypt, since those who had gone there against the command of God ought not to have the protection of the Lord there. Mystically, however, the name of the Lord is not called by the mouth of heretics in the land of Egypt: because neither their speech nor prayer, while they are in error, is acceptable to God. For praise is not comely in the mouth of a sinner, Ecclesiasticus 15. Those therefore who persevere in error will perish by the sword of strict judgment. But those who, leaving error, return penitent from Egypt to the land of Judah: and thereafter holding the Catholic faith will be saved.
45.1: 45.1 The word that Jeremiah spoke, etc. Baruch, still unpracticed in bearing the sufferings which he was to experience, was afraid of the calamity of captivity which was impending in the time of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, hence he complains that sorrow was added to his sorrow, to whom the Lord answered that he seeks peace superfluously, when the whole people labors under the burden of tribulations. It signifies, however, those who in the pressure of tribulations or persecutions, by which the Church is burdened in the present, waver from faint-heartedness, seeking the consolation that is promised in the future. Hence: You shall be made sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy, John 16.
46.1: 46.1 The word which was made, etc. RABANUS. Thus far the prophet treated mixedly of Judah and Israel, of the Chaldeans and Egyptians, for the fitness of the narrative, etc., down to the year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah when Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt fought at Carchemish with Nebuchadnezzar and was overcome.
46.9: 46.9 Get up on the horses. THE SAME. Heretics and schismatics sprung from various provinces vainly dispose wars against the city of God, etc., down to when they are delivered into the hands of him who set his throne toward the north, that he may cast them into the pool of fire and brimstone.
46.11: 46.11 Go up into Gilead. JEROME. It is a mountain to which on the seventh day Jacob came, fleeing from Haran: it is behind Phoenicia and Arabia, joined to the hills of Lebanon, and extends through the desert as far as beyond the Jordan where Sihon king of the Amorites dwelt. It fell to the lot of the sons of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh. Take balm. RABANUS. The Greeks call, for it is so called from what flows, etc., down to because they will not receive health from them, but confusion.
46.12: 46.12 The nations have heard. THE SAME. Because the comfort of the idols being frustrated, etc., down to they receive not the victory of truth, but, captives to error, fall alike into the pit of perdition.
46.14: 46.14 Declare to Egypt. As if to say: You who have heard my prophecy, tell Pharaoh that the time and tumult of war is at hand.
46.18: 46.18 As Tabor. This is from the comparison of fruitful places, as it were drowned in the sea, you can understand the great ruin of the Egyptians. JEROME. Tabor is the boundary of Zebulun, a mountain in the middle of the plain of Galilee, lofty with a wonderful roundness: ten miles from Diocaesarea toward the east. Carmel, which was also the boundary between the tribes of Issachar and Naphtali, where Nabal the Carmelite was, and now there is a village named Carmela, at the tenth stone from the town of Hebron, inclining to the eastern quarter where there is a Roman garrison. RABANUS. Mystically, however, because Tabor, etc., down to sunk in the sea of this age, and in perpetual damnation.
46.20: 46.20 A heifer. Because the Egyptian people, nourished in delights, untamed, wanton, refused the yoke of discipline.
46.21: 46.21 Hirelings. RABANUS. He calls the princes of the Egyptians not shepherds but hirelings, etc., down to But the hireling, and he that is not the shepherd, when he sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep and flees, John 10.
46.26: 46.26 And after this, etc. THE SAME. Though it seems to intimate that the kingdom of the Egyptians was not irreparably destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, etc., down to: The Lord shall strike Egypt with a plague and heal it, Isaiah 19., etc.
46.27: 46.27 And fear not you, etc. This promise does not well suit the Jews: who, dispersed through the whole world, etc., down to: Because blindness in part has happened in Israel, and when the fullness of the Gentiles shall have come in, then all Israel shall be saved, Romans 11.
47.1: 47.1 The word which was made, etc. Jeremiah, like Isaiah and Ezekiel, predicts plagues to come upon the neighboring nations, because they harassed the people of God and rejoiced in his adversity. To the Palestinians, therefore, as before to the Egyptians, he foretells captivity to come.
47.4: 47.4 And shall be destroyed. He shows that Tyre and Sidon belong to the Palestinians, though Tyre fell by lot to Naphtali, and Sidon, the boundary of the Canaanites, to Asher: but he did not possess it, because he could not drive out the enemies. The remnant of the island of Cappadocia. In which the Cappadocians dwelt, the former inhabitants having been slain. This is the boundary of the Canaanites near Egypt, and fell by lot to Judah: but he did not obtain it, because the Anakim, that is the giants of the Philistines, resisted most strongly: and it is to this day a notable city of Palestine, although it was prophesied of it, Gaza shall be a heap forever: but where it first was scarcely any traces remain, for it was built in another place.
47.5: 47.5 Baldness is come, etc. RABANUS. He signifies that a plague is coming upon heretics and schismatics and all enemies of the Church, etc., down to For by lust of the flesh it burns minds: but at the last it will be cast down.
47.7: 47.7 How shall it be quiet, etc. As if to say: The sword cannot be quiet unless the Lord commands, whose vengeance it executes; or: As from the person of the afflicted he had spoken to the sword of the Lord, but here he answers in his own person.
48.1: 48.1 To Moab thus says the Lord, etc. RABANUS. As there is circumcision carnal and spiritual, so there is Moab carnal and spiritual. Moab is interpreted, etc., down to Moab is a province of the Arabs, Nebo a noble city, in which was Chemosh the idol, which is also Baal-peor.
48.6: 48.6 Save your souls. Those who wish to save their soul, let them flee the crooked doctrine of philosophers and heretics, where destruction is sure: and by the humility of confession do penance for error in the desert of strict abstinence, and abide in the simplicity and truth of Catholic doctrine.
48.9: 48.9 Give a flower, etc. He who seemed to flourish by human invention and in secular knowledge shall be reduced to desert and solitude. Because all hypocrisy displeases God, as the following sentence shows:
48.10: 48.10 Cursed be he that does, etc. For it is necessary that we consider not only what we do, but with what discretion we do it. Cursed. RABANUS. Sloth is born from torpor, fraud from private affection, etc., down to often through the intervention of sloth they fail, and love growing cold they waste away. And cursed. This curse can suit all who follow the flux of the age, and neglect to chastise their bodies and bring them into servitude, according to that: They that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, Galatians 5., etc. Because without shedding of blood there is no remission of sins. For flesh and blood shall not possess the kingdom of God, 1 Corinthians 15. Cursed therefore is he who keeps back the sword, that is the word of God, from blood: by which, namely, the matter of sins is animated; whatever in our members has grown carnal and earthly is to be shed and cut off by the sword of the word of God. GREGORY. To keep the sword from blood is to withhold the word of preaching from the killing of the carnal life, of which it is said: My sword shall devour flesh, Isaiah 1. Hence Paul says, I take you to witness this day that I am clean from the blood of all men. For I have not spared to declare unto you all the counsel of God, Acts 10.
48.11: 48.11 Fruitful. Moab is shown to have come from abundance into hatred and elation, and to have despised the afflicted people of God, because it suffered nothing of affliction or captivity.
48.12: 48.12 I will send to him, etc. RABANUS. Whoever trust in human philosophy, despising the faith and simple doctrine of the Church, etc., down to then they shall go with the devil and his angels into everlasting fire. But the just into life everlasting.
48.17: 48.17 Comfort him. Ironically, or he provokes to penance, that by fitting satisfaction they may escape misery. Mystically. The wise of this world and heretics, whom Moab signifies, if they do not correct their folly converted to the Catholic faith, ruin and devastation will come upon all their cities, that is diverse sects. For those which are far or near from the truth shall be overthrown, the Gospel shining.
48.25: 48.25 Cut off. JEROME. As he prophesied against Babylon and the Philistines, etc., down to whatever belongs to earthly knowledge and is thought strong is overthrown, so that nothing is approved which was thought most strong.
48.29: 48.29 We have heard. Because in the former verse he provoked the erring to penance, and warned them to be converted to Christ, that they might remain forever in his faith; now, recognizing very many incorrigible and obstinate, in the person of those who were saved from Moab and by their experience learned its pride, he says: We have heard the pride of Moab, etc. And he charges Moab with pride, because it is elated more than its strength can or does require.
48.31: 48.31 Therefore I will howl for Moab. He shows the power of former felicity and the blow of sudden overthrow. For Moab all I will cry. Which is interpreted their strength, and signifies the strongest dogmas of heretics built up dialectically, in which seemed to be the strength of error.
48.32: 48.32 I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. The storm of this age. For he seems to signify that some of Moab wish to be converted to the Lord. For Sibmah is interpreted some conversion. The vine of Sibmah, etc. Lifting up the height, because pride strives to raise a tower to heaven.
48.34: 48.34 From Zoar to Horonaim. Zoar is a city overhanging the Dead Sea, where the boundary of the Moabites is. He indicates therefore that the wailing will sound to the farthest bounds of the province. Of which Isaiah: Its bars as far as Zoar a heifer of three years, Isaiah 15., that is of perfect age. For as in men the thirtieth year, so in cattle and beasts of burden the third year is the strongest. The waters also of Nimrim. Isaiah: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate, Isaiah 15., etc. And what is here less said is fully expounded in Isaiah. For Nimrim is a town above the Dead Sea.
48.35: 48.35 And I will take away from Moab. The sect of human wisdom perishing, the pomp and clamor of words has ceased, so that neither philosophers nor heretics who have gone out from the Church find anything in their doctrine that is useful for human life.
48.37: 48.37 For every head shall be bald. RABANUS. Among the ancients the shaving of the beard and head was a sign of mourning, etc., down to hence Isaiah: On all its heads baldness, every beard shall be shaven, Isaiah 15.
48.38: 48.38 Because I have broken Moab. All the doctrine of philosophers and heretics, because it is fragile and useless, is crushed and scattered by the truth.
48.41: 48.41 And the heart of the strong men of Moab shall be. Well he compares the heart of Moab to the heart of a woman in labor; because from great luxury one comes to great sorrow.
48.45: 48.45 In the shadow of Heshbon they stood. Because in its fortification it hoped for comfort for itself, but in vain: because the fire of vengeance consumed the head of the tumult of the sons of Moab, the just judge repaying.
48.46: 48.46 Woe to you, Moab. Because neither the fortification of cities nor the power of idols could defend you: so shall there be perpetual woe to those who trust in human wisdom and serve diverse errors.
48.47: 48.47 And I will bring back the captivity of Moab. It seems to signify the time of grace, in which whoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, Joel 2.
49.1: 49.1 To the children. After Moab, the words are turned to the children of Ammon, and they are rebuked, that they dared to invade the land of Israel, whence a fitting vengeance is foretold to them, and Israel is predicted to possess its possessors.
49.2: 49.2 Daughters of Rabbah. The metropolis of the Moabites, now called Ariopolis, a compound name from Hebrew and Greek, that is, the city of Mars.
49.6: 49.6 And after this. Because after the conversion of heretics to the right faith, the captivity of sin will be dissolved, they will be received into the communion of the Church from which they had gone out. And captives. By the children of Ammon, who were begotten of Lot in a cave and in drunkenness and incest, we can take heretics, according to that, They went out from us, but they were not of us, John 2.
49.7: 49.7 To Edom. RABANUS. Tropologically Edom is earthly and fleshly delight, which rises against the spirit, that we do not the things that are of the spirit, and the soul, etc., down to For when the flesh shall have been subjected to the spirit, Edom shall pass into Judea, and the flesh shall serve reason.
49.9: 49.9 If thieves. Heretics who steal what suffices for themselves, and daily snatch some from the Church, entering the vineyard of the Lord which he transplanted out of Egypt, desire to lay waste all, so that they scarcely leave a gleaning in it. But the Lord on the contrary brings into the midst all their secrets, and those of the patriarchs of Esau (who found the first heresies) the ecclesiastical men and teachers. And the first victory is to lay open what was covered. JEROME. The discourse was made against the Jews, who envy the Christians, etc., down to that mortifying our members (fornication, namely, uncleanness and the like) we may obtain eternal victory in Christ.
49.14: 49.14 I have heard. This sentence is contained in Obadiah in almost the same words, and much of this chapter.
49.15: 49.15 For behold. RABANUS. As if to say: O Edom, who are the least among all the nations round about, etc., down to thence I would draw you, and bring you back to the land of the other nations. I have made you small among the nations. O heretic, though you seem great to yourself, and despise the littleness of the Church, yet you are small and contemptible.
49.16: 49.16 When you shall be exalted, etc. RABANUS. Because heretics promise themselves the height and likeness of eagles, which are gathered to the Lord's carcass, etc., down to What is said against heretics and the flesh can also be understood against the Jews.
49.19: 49.19 Behold as a lion. THE SAME. As the Lord chastised the pride of the Jews, whom through the Jordan, etc., down to but a most savage lion will thrust them down into hell to be tormented perpetually.
49.21: 49.21 At the voice of the fall, etc. The ravager coming, the din of their fall will resound far and wide, striking terror into the neighboring provinces.
49.23: 49.23 Confounded. RABANUS. After the Philistines, Moabites, Ammonites also and Idumeans, to Damascus, that is Arabia, etc., down to for when the people of the Jews was taken, Damascus, which Aretas ruled, was likewise taken.
49.24: 49.24 Dissolved. Damascus is interpreted cup of blood, or drinking blood, or blood of sackcloth; all which suit the heathen, etc., down to For as a heap of stones is gathered from scattered stones, so from all nations a heap of believers is gathered in the ruin of the Jews falling while the Gentiles rise.
49.28: 49.28 To Kedar. These are Hagarenes, but with a usurped name are called Saracens, and dwell through the whole wilderness, of whom the poet says: And the Agi wandering widely. RABANUS. Mystically. Kedar, which is interpreted darkness, and Hazor, etc., down to who pretend to be children of the East, when they are children of darkness.
49.29: 49.29 Tents. All these properly signify the nation of the Saracens, who dwell in tents, and where night overtakes them they have their seat, and many herds and flocks and droves of camels; but they have no doors nor bars, for they dwell not in cities but in solitude. All these were destroyed by the Babylonians.
49.35: 49.35 Behold I will break, etc. RABANUS. Elam a region of Persia, whence the Elamites. For the prophet predicts, etc., down to The Elamites also are interpreted despising or tempting, and signify persecutors of the Church.
50.1: 50.1 The word. The prophecy against Egypt, the Philistines, Moab, the children of Ammon, Damascus too and Kedar being finished, the discourse is directed against Babylon and the Chaldeans; that those whom he before reproved covertly, now, openly manifesting their crimes, he may plainly proclaim that devastation and desolation follow, Isaiah also and Ezekiel prophesied similar things against the Babylonians and Chaldeans.
50.2: 50.2 They are confounded. Isaiah says similar things: Behold I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not seek silver nor desire gold, Isaiah 13.
50.4: 50.4 The children of Israel shall come. RABANUS. This promise signifies the return of the people of God from captivity, etc., down to that they may be joined to him in an everlasting covenant.
50.6: 50.6 My people have been a lost flock. By this sentence are marked the kings of the Israelites, who made the people err and turn aside to idolatry: of whom the first was Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made the golden calves to be adored: then the other transgressors of the law.
50.8: 50.8 Depart, etc. According to the history he warns the Israelites, who were to be taken captive into Babylon, that they not think they would have a stable possession there, but have the hope of returning, and when the captivity should be relaxed, flee from there: because it was to come to pass that it should be laid waste by the Medes and Persians. ORIGEN. As our body stands in some place of the earth, so the soul, according to its state, is in some place of the earth by name. Our body, etc., down to so in Egypt, one is in Tahpanhes, another is in Memphis, another dwells in Syene, another in Bubastis.
50.12: 50.12 Your mother is exceedingly confounded, etc. Isaiah says the like, And Babylon, that glorious one in kingdoms, the glory of the Chaldeans' pride, shall be overthrown as the Lord overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, Isaiah 13. Behold the last shall be, etc. At the end of the world, or at the death of each, all the glory and pride of the Chaldeans and the confusion of the world shall depart from us, and so all things shall be overthrown, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, nor shall there be any more a state of pleasure or of the world.
50.15: 50.15 As she has done, do to her. That is, as she by Nebuchadnezzar laid waste the nations round about, so render her retribution.
50.16: 50.16 From the face of the sword of the dove. The dove is called foolish, because she nurses another's young; so Nebuchadnezzar by oppressing and cherishing others. He calls even Nebuchadnezzar a dove, not for simplicity but for the folly of pride.
50.17: 50.17 The lions have cast out, etc. Tiglath-pileser, who carried a great part of the Jews into Assyria, and Sennacherib, who led the ten tribes into the mountains of the Medes, these are called lions.
50.18: 50.18 Behold I will visit. RABANUS. The Lord visits the king of Babylon, that is of confusion, as he visited the king of Assyria, which is interpreted, etc., down to but a new people in a new city shall exult forever.
50.21: 50.21 Over the land of the rulers. It is commanded to the preachers of Christ that they strive to overturn the kingdom of the devil: and his malignant works and worst counsels, that they may slay all the sinners of the earth, and destroy from the city of the Lord all that work iniquity.
50.23: 50.23 How is broken, etc. ORIGEN. The hammer of the whole earth is the devil. But there is one who cares not for the hammer of the whole earth, a man, namely, standing on adamantine walls, etc., down to for it is not subject to the law of God, neither can it be, and Babylon was found and taken: because she resisted the Lord.
50.25: 50.25 The Lord has opened his treasure, etc. THE SAME. Another edition: Open her storehouses, etc., as the Apostle says, Romans 6.: He endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction, to make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, etc. Some then are vessels of mercy, others vessels of wrath, etc., down to who asserts that the stars are not the causes of what happens on earth, especially of what befalls Christians: he carries out the commandment of the Lord.
50.28: 50.28 The voice of those who flee. ORIGEN. Would that this were our voice, O catechumens, of those fleeing from Babylon, and fleeing, etc., down to kill all the sinners of the earth who are in you, and all the Babylonians, that cleansed you may pass over into Jerusalem the city of God.
50.31: 50.31 Behold I am against you. RABANUS. Mystically he foretells Antichrist, who shall be exalted above all that is called God, etc., down to because they feared not to inflict calumny and captivity on the people of God.
50.37: 50.37 And they shall be as women. THE SAME. Unwarlike as women, through the Medes and Persians he destroyed them, etc., down to because their synagogue is a land of graven things, and they glory in portents, that is false figments.
50.44: 50.44 Behold as a lion. THE SAME. He seems to signify that Nebuchadnezzar, after the kingdom of the Jews, etc., down to and to show that it was done not by the power of Cyrus but by the judgment of the Lord, it is added: For who is like me?
51.5: 51.5 For was not, etc. Because the Lord sent them for vengeance of his people, whom he chastised not by correcting but crushed by raging: hence, Woe to Assyria, the rod of my fury, Isaiah 10.
51.6: 51.6 Flee out of the midst, etc. After the plagues of Babylon, he turns the exhortation to the Jews historically, to the faithful mystically, that they flee out of the midst of Babylon, that is of worldly confusion. ORIGEN. Not by degrees, not step by step, but quickly go out, whoever have a confused soul, etc., down to Likewise, when sins are lesser, God uses ministers: but when graver, then he himself hastens to retribution.
51.7: 51.7 A golden cup, etc. The cup of Babylon is not always golden nor in the hand of the Lord; for when it comes to vengeance and is placed in the hand of the Lord, the land will become what it was made in Job. Nor is it continually held in the hand of the Lord; but then only when the Lord will restore to her what she deserves. ORIGEN. A golden cup. Nebuchadnezzar, wishing to deceive men by the cup of Babylon, did not mix it in an earthen vessel, etc., down to I have often seen a golden cup in the beautiful ornament of speech, and considering the poisons of doctrines I found it the cup of Babylon. Making drunk, etc. THE SAME. See all men drunk; we are drunk with anger and sadness: we are drunk, etc., down to by him we are all made drunk as long as we are earth. Of the wine. THE SAME. As in those who drink bodily wine beyond measure we see the motion of a drunken body, etc., down to the nations have drunk, therefore they are moved.
51.8: 51.8 Suddenly is fallen. It signifies the consummation of the world to come suddenly, which will be not by parts but at once, as Jericho falling quickly or suddenly perished. If, however, you come to the coming of Christ, and see his great work, how he overthrew all the dogmas of the Gentiles to free believers from the yoke of error, you will see that in his passion Babylon suddenly fell and was crushed; let each see Babylon fallen in his own breast. In whose heart it has not fallen, Christ has not yet come to him: Babylon falls, Jerusalem the holy city of God is built. Howl. JEROME. Because no soul is incurable with God, he gives counsel to those who can, etc., down to but because she would not be cured, the good physicians make satisfaction and say:
51.9: 51.9 We have cured. ORIGEN. See that God does not sometimes command the angels to make remedies for your languishing soul, etc., down to God brings forth his judgment to humble what is exalted.
51.16: 51.16 Who lifts up the clouds, that is the preachers and prophets, who defend us from the heat of the future judgment by the rain of their speech, when they bring forth things to come. Lightnings. The preachers of the prophets are lightnings when they strike enemies: rains when they wash the devout from sins and pour the shower of salvation: whence spiritual fruits may sprout and ripen into a mature harvest. And brings forth the winds out of his treasures. The winds are the apostles, whose preaching runs through the world like a very swift wind: of whom elsewhere it is said: He made his arrows for them that burn, Psalm 7. Wings are given to the very winds on account of the speed of running about; hence: He flew upon the wings of the winds, ibid. 11.
51.17: 51.17 Every man is become a fool. Well after the overthrow of Babylon he reproves the makers of idols, because by the folly of the human mind vain works worthy of laughter were made: because neither is there spirit in them, nor voice, nor any efficacy: hence they can free neither themselves nor their worshipers in the day of visitation. Confounded. RABANUS. The overthrow of Babylon being shown, the prophet returns to the author of so great a judgment: because there is no power but from God, who rules in the kingdom of men, and to whom he will gives it.
51.25: 51.25 Behold I, etc. The pestilent mountain, Nebuchadnezzar, and the kingdom of the Chaldeans; or the devil, who elsewhere is called a dark mountain, because of the darkness of error. And I will give you. To this mountain belong Jews, heretics, blasphemers, and all the impious, who persist in malice and are not converted to become living stones in the building of God.
51.30: 51.30 They have ceased, etc. Cyrus and Darius coming, the strength of Babylon and of her princes ceased.
51.33: 51.33 The daughter of Babylon, etc. The people of Babylon was, when by the power of the kingdom and abundance of riches it threshed and crushed the nations: but the time of her harvest has come when she is compelled to receive what she has done, of whom in the person of the Jewish people it is consequently said: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has eaten me up and devoured me. And I will make her sea a desert, etc. RABANUS. Mystically the sea signifies the turbulence of this age, which the Lord makes a desert. For he will make its luxury cease, and the wicked will be scattered, who served the confusion of errors and vices.
51.41: 51.41 How is Sheshach taken. RABANUS. Sheshach is interpreted linen of a sack, or hand of a sack: as Babylon confusion, etc., down to that they go out from their society, lest they perish with them.
51.45: 51.45 Go out of the midst of her. THE SAME. He who wishes to save his soul, etc., down to but in meditation on his law and the exercise of virtues vigorous.
51.52: 51.52 Therefore, etc. THE SAME. He enumerates the plagues coming upon Babylon and her nobles, leaders and magistrates, and all the people, etc., down to Go out of her, my people, that you be not partakers of her sins, and that you receive not of her plagues, Apocalypse 18., etc.
51.64: 51.64 Thus shall Babylon sink. For according to the history Babylon was sunk in the Euphrates, though reduced to solitude. But he foretells the eternal destruction of spiritual Babylon, which will be plunged into the depth of hell with the prince the devil. Hence John: A mighty angel took up a stone as it were a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying: With such violence shall Babylon be thrown down, Apocalypse 18.
52.1: 52.1 Son of twenty-one. The history which relates the capture of Zedekiah and the laying waste of Jerusalem by the Chaldeans is contained fully in the book of Kings.
52.4: 52.4 And it came to pass. The number nine, less than ten, signifies the imperfection of the law, etc., down to enclosed by the darkness of sins they flee, and seeing the wolf coming they leave the sheep.
52.7: 52.7 By the way of the gate. He covertly reproves the sloth of teachers, who, placed between the walls of the two Testaments, seek not to wage war but to escape, and to abound in delights (which the garden signifies) rather than resist enemies with the shield of faith.

52.24: 52.24 And the captain took, etc. The devil deceives and takes captive even the strong in the Church; hence: His food is choice, Habakkuk 1., etc.
52.25: 52.25 Out of the city he took, etc. The continent, namely, not having in their breast the oil of grace and mercy (like the foolish virgins), who are vainly set over warriors when they do not premeditate to avoid arrogance.
52.26: 52.26 Seven men, etc. Sanctified by the sevenfold Spirit, namely. And sixty men, etc. Foolish, namely, coworkers, who rightly are called by the name of the common sort, who neglected to discern and fulfill the usefulness of divine counsel.
52.27: 52.27 And the king of Babylon struck them, etc. This the king of Babylon seeks, that those whom he has plucked from the Church he may bring to the slaughter of perpetual death.
